content_html:
Former Ukrainian defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov reveals struggles to secure Patriot missiles and Western support

Former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has opened up about the challenges he faced assembling Patriot missiles during his first meeting at the “Ramstein” contact group. He described how European stockpiles of air defense systems were desperately low, sharing that it was a struggle to collect just 20 missiles-until Germany added another five to the mix. Fedorov, now weeks after his resignation, spoke about the difficulties of securing missile defense support from Western partners-and offered his candid thoughts on the political pressures Kyiv faces to defend itself while those same partners hold back on aid.

Fedorov’s comments came during a wide-ranging interview with activist and volunteer Serhiy Sternenko, published on YouTube on the evening of July 6. Beyond the issues of missile defense and the war itself, Fedorov highlighted the limited authority of Ukraine’s acting defense minister, who cannot fully participate in government decision-making. He also outlined a three-pronged war strategy and discussed the mounting pressure from anonymous Telegram channels.

Asked about the shipments of Patriot missiles to Ukraine-an area where he said partner countries have applied pressure-Fedorov clarified that there is a program called PURL, under which the U.S. sells missile defense systems to Ukraine using European funds. Supplies are tight, but deliveries have come in at a steady, albeit limited, pace. The core problem, he said, is that Russia’s weekly and monthly ballistic strike rates are outpacing U.S. production capacity, which also has to satisfy domestic needs.

Reflecting on his first “Ramstein” meeting as defense minister, Fedorov recalled how he and then-NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte went table-to-table, appealing directly to each partner nation’s defense minister for just one or two missiles each-whatever they could spare. He said European reserves ranged from just 5 or 10 to, at best, 50 missiles per country. They struck a deal with German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius to add five more, but only if they managed to collect a total of 20 from everyone else.

“It worked,” Fedorov recounted. “We also signed a contract with Germany for hundreds of PAC-2 missiles, but those will arrive next year as they are newly produced. We’re taking those on credit-this is the first contract of its kind.”

At the start of the interview, Fedorov addressed another challenge: Ukraine’s parliament had gone on break without appointing a permanent new defense minister. He pointed out that the acting minister, in accordance with Ukrainian law, has no voting rights at government meetings, effectively sidelining them in the decision-making process. The conversation also touched on his battles with weapon-industry lobbying within the Ministry of Defense and a wave of attacks from anonymous social media channels. Fedorov then outlined his three-part plan for the war, focused on “Air. Land. Economy.”

“The ideal outcome is ballistic missile against ballistic missile,” Fedorov said. “There are other operations, and they need to be conducted aggressively and symmetrically so that Russian forces understand: just moving a launcher into range is almost a guaranteed death sentence.”

Fedorov resigned as defense minister on July 16, citing disagreements with then-Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi and General Staff. President Volodymyr Zelensky replaced Syrskyi with Mykhailo Drapatyi. Fedorov later revealed there were other deep internal issues within the Defense Ministry, where he had attempted to root out entrenched arms lobbying.

Reports surfaced in July that Fedorov was being considered for new positions, both by President Zelensky and by Italy’s Ministry of Defense.

content_html_zh:
乌克兰前国防部长米哈伊洛·费多罗夫透露为获得爱国者导弹和西方支持而付出的努力

乌克兰前国防部长米哈伊洛·费多罗夫在“拉姆施泰因”联络小组的第一次会议上公开了他在组装爱国者导弹方面面临的挑战。 他描述了欧洲防空系统库存的严重程度，并表示收集 20 枚导弹非常困难，直到德国又增加了 5 枚。 费多罗夫在辞职几周后谈到了从西方伙伴那里获得导弹防御支持的困难，并坦率地表达了他对基辅面临的自卫政治压力而这些伙伴却拒绝援助的看法。

费多罗夫是在对活动家兼志愿者 Serhiy Sternenko 进行广泛采访时发表上述言论的，该采访于 7 月 6 日晚在 YouTube 上发布。 除了导弹防御和战争本身的问题之外，费多罗夫还强调了乌克兰代理国防部长的权力有限，他无法充分参与政府决策。 他还概述了三管齐下的战争战略，并讨论了来自匿名电报频道日益增加的压力。

当被问及向乌克兰运送爱国者导弹一事时，费多罗夫澄清说，有一个名为“PURL”的计划，根据该计划，美国利用欧洲资金向乌克兰出售导弹防御系统。 供应紧张，但交货速度虽然有限，但却稳定。 他说，核心问题是俄罗斯每周和每月的弹道打击率超过了美国的生产能力，而美国的生产能力还必须满足国内需求。

费多罗夫在回顾他作为国防部长的第一次“拉姆施泰因”会议时，回忆起他和时任北约秘书长马克·吕特是如何逐桌直接呼吁每个伙伴国国防部长提供一到两枚导弹的——无论他们有多少多余的。 他说，欧洲的储备数量从每个国家仅有 5 或 10 枚到最多 50 枚导弹不等。 他们与德国国防部长鲍里斯·皮斯托利斯（Boris Pistorius）达成协议，再增加 5 个，但前提是他们能从其他人那里筹集到总共 20 个。

“它起作用了，”费多罗夫回忆道。 “我们还与德国签署了数百枚 PAC-2 导弹的合同，但这些导弹将于明年抵达，因为它们是新生产的。 我们正在赊购这些合同——这是第一份此类合同。”

在采访开始时，费多罗夫谈到了另一个挑战：乌克兰议会已经休会，但没有任命一位永久的新国防部长。 他指出，根据乌克兰法律，代理部长在政府会议上没有投票权，这实际上使他们在决策过程中处于边缘地位。 谈话还谈到了他与国防部内部武器行业游说的斗争以及来自匿名社交媒体渠道的一波攻击。 费多罗夫随后概述了他的战争计划，分为三部分，重点是“空气”。 土地。 经济。”

费多罗夫说：“理想的结果是弹道导弹对抗弹道导弹。” “还有其他行动，需要积极、对称地进行，以便俄罗斯军队明白：仅仅将发射器移入射程就几乎等于被判死刑。”

费多罗夫于 7 月 16 日辞去国防部长职务，理由是与时任总司令亚历山大·西尔斯基 (Oleksandr Syrskyi) 和总参谋部存在分歧。 总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基用米哈伊洛·德拉帕蒂取代了西尔斯基。 费多罗夫后来透露，国防部内部还存在其他深层问题，他曾试图根除根深蒂固的军备游说活动。

7 月有报道称，泽连斯基总统和意大利国防部正在考虑让费多罗夫担任新职务。
